nodes.label: Cloud E-commerce Platform
nodes.rationale: Full-stack e-commerce demo: Next.js storefront + Spring Boot API behind Nginx, orchestrated by Docker Compose. Chosen so the whole stack runs from a single `docker compose up --build` with one public entrypoint.

nodes.label: Nginx Reverse Proxy (:80/:443)
nodes.rationale: Single ingress: `/` routes to the frontend and `/api/` rewrites to the backend, so the browser only ever talks to one origin (avoids CORS and exposes one TLS cert).

nodes.label: JWT Authentication & Admin Seeding
nodes.rationale: JWT with role support plus an auto-seeded admin user (EMAIL_ADMIN / PASSWORD_ADMIN) so a fresh deployment always has an admin able to manage products.

nodes.label: Server-side Cart Persistence & Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Cart lives server-side (not in localStorage) so it survives device switches; a scheduled job cleans up abandoned carts to keep the table bounded.

nodes.label: Region-based Shipping Quotes
nodes.rationale: Flat rates per Brazilian macro-region resolved from the CEP — avoids integrating a live carrier API while still producing plausible shipping costs.

nodes.label: MP_WEBHOOK_SECRET (webhook signature verification)
nodes.rationale: Signing secret used to verify POST /order/webhook. Blank => signature check is skipped with a warning, so local/demo runs work without a secret; required in prod for real payments.

nodes.label: APP_BASE_URL (public HTTPS base)
nodes.rationale: One variable drives three derived values: the frontend's NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, the Mercado Pago webhook notification URL, and the MP back URLs — so a domain change is a one-line edit.

nodes.label: APP_SEED_DEMO_DATA (demo dataset seeding)
nodes.rationale: Seeds products/users/orders on startup for a resume/portfolio demo. Idempotent — skips if products already exist — so restarts don't duplicate data. Default false.

nodes.label: DDL_AUTO (Hibernate schema strategy)
nodes.rationale: Defaults to `validate` in prod to prevent accidental schema mutation; must be flipped to `update` on a fresh demo DB so the schema exists before the seeder runs.

nodes.label: PAYMENTS_DEMO_MODE (simulated approved payment)
nodes.rationale: Skips Mercado Pago at checkout and simulates an approved payment (order PAID, stock decremented, cart cleared) so demos run without a real MP token.

nodes.label: E-commerce REST API
nodes.rationale: Backend handling users, products, categories, carts and payments, explicitly optimized for performance, resilience and fault tolerance.

nodes.label: Controller / Service / Repository Layering
nodes.rationale: Classic three-tier split: Controller = HTTP, Service = business rules, Repository = data access. Keeps business rules testable independently of the web layer.

nodes.label: JWT Auth with Refresh Token Strategy
nodes.rationale: Short-lived JWT with expiration plus a refresh token, so a leaked access token has a bounded blast radius.
nodes.norm_label: jwt auth with refresh token strategy

nodes.label: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
nodes.rationale: Endpoints are tiered Public / JWT / Admin; write operations on products and categories are ADMIN-only while cart and order endpoints only need any authenticated user.

nodes.label: BCrypt Password Hashing
nodes.rationale: Passwords are hashed with BCrypt before persistence so a DB dump never exposes plaintext credentials.

nodes.label: N+1 Query Avoidance via JPA Fetch Strategies
nodes.rationale: JPA fetch strategies and explicit joins are used instead of lazy per-row loading, because listing endpoints would otherwise fan out one query per product/image row.
nodes.norm_label: n+1 query avoidance via jpa fetch strategies

nodes.label: Pagination on Listing Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Spring Pageable params (page/size/sort) on GET /product and GET /order to prevent unbounded payloads.

nodes.label: S3 Object Storage for Product Images
nodes.rationale: Images are offloaded to S3 rather than the DB/filesystem so the API stays stateless and containers remain disposable.
nodes.norm_label: s3 object storage for product images

nodes.label: Dedicated IAM User (Least Privilege)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated IAM user restricted to only the required S3 resources, so leaked AWS credentials cannot touch anything else in the account. Sensitive values come from .env, never source.

nodes.label: Cart Consistency Handling
nodes.rationale: Planned in CartService#getOrCreateCart: detect products that became unavailable while the cart sat idle and surface that to the UI, rather than failing at checkout.

nodes.label: Mercado Pago Integration (checkout + webhook)
nodes.rationale: POST /order/{userId} creates a checkout and returns the MP URL; POST /order/webhook is public because Mercado Pago calls it server-to-server.

nodes.label: Planned Redis Caching Layer
nodes.rationale: Listed as a future improvement to improve read performance; not yet implemented.

nodes.label: Planned Event-Driven Architecture (Kafka)
nodes.rationale: Listed as a future improvement for scalability; the current design is synchronous request/response.

nodes.label: AWS S3 Config (region sa-east-1, bucket spring-s3-user)
nodes.norm_label: aws s3 config (region sa-east-1, bucket spring-s3-user)

nodes.label: Multipart Upload Limits (10MB)
nodes.rationale: max-file-size and max-request-size both capped at 10MB, bounding the memory/S3 cost of a single product-image upload.

nodes.label: Maven Parent POM Overrides
nodes.rationale: The project POM declares empty <license> and <developers> elements purely to block unwanted inheritance from the Spring Boot parent POM. Removing them is only correct if the parent is swapped and inheritance is actually wanted.

nodes.label: Full-Stack Docker Compose Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Four services on one private `app-network`: only nginx publishes ports (80/443); postgres, backend and frontend are unreachable from outside the network.

nodes.label: nginx service (commerce-nginx)
nodes.rationale: Mounts nginx.conf and /etc/letsencrypt read-only, and is the only service binding host ports.

nodes.label: INTERNAL_API_URL (SSR split-horizon API base)
nodes.rationale: Server-side (SSR) calls hit http://commerce-api:8080 on the internal network because the container cannot reach its own public domain; browser-side calls use the public NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL built from APP_BASE_URL. This split fixed the server-rendering bug.

nodes.label: Local-only Postgres (postgres-local, :5432)
nodes.rationale: Standalone Postgres with hardcoded commerce/postgres/postgres credentials and a published 5432 port, so `./mvnw spring-boot:run` on the host has a DB without booting the whole stack.

nodes.label: Server-Component Fetch / Client-Component Interactivity
nodes.rationale: Server Components in app/ fetch data (axios or fetch with next: { revalidate }) and pass it as props into "use client" components, which own interactivity, cart operations and auth-gated content. Keeps data fetching off the client bundle.

nodes.label: AuthContext (JWT auth state)
nodes.rationale: On mount reads localStorage token, sets api.defaults.headers.common['Authorization'], then calls GET /users/me to rehydrate the user. Token in localStorage + a globally-injected axios header means every caller is authenticated without threading the token through props.

nodes.label: Optimistic Cart Mutations with Rollback
nodes.rationale: addItem/updateQuantity/removeItem/clearCart update local state immediately and roll back on API error, with sonner toasts — cart state is authoritative server-side but the UI must not wait on a round trip.

nodes.label: Provider Nesting (AuthProvider > CartProvider > Navbar)
nodes.rationale: CartProvider must nest inside AuthProvider because it needs the user id from AuthContext to fetch GET /cart/:userId. Footer is deliberately rendered outside the providers.

nodes.label: primitives/ Design-System Atoms
nodes.rationale: Thin wrappers over Radix UI / Vaul (Button, Card, Input, Label, Separator, Sheet, Drawer, Skeleton, Badge, Avatar) — the atoms that components/ composes into product cards, cart UI and navbar.

nodes.label: Allowed Remote Image Hosts (next.config.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Only images.unsplash.com (demo/seed imagery) and cloud-commerce-stack.s3.sa-east-1.amazonaws.com (real product uploads) are whitelisted for next/image.

nodes.label: create-next-app Bootstrap Notes
nodes.rationale: Untouched create-next-app boilerplate (mentions Geist font and Vercel deploy) — superseded in practice by front-end/CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Airbnb Design System Analysis
nodes.rationale: A token-based extraction (colors / typography / rounded / spacing / components) of Airbnb's consumer-marketplace system, kept as a structure-only reference.

nodes.label: Rausch (#ff385c) — Single Brand Voltage
nodes.rationale: One accent color carries every primary CTA, the search orb, the heart save state and brand links. Used scarcely — pages are ~90% white + ink with one or two Rausch moments — which is what makes it recognizable.

nodes.label: Airbnb Cereal VF Type Scale
nodes.rationale: A single variable font carries display, body, nav and micro copy — no separate display family. Display weights stay modest (500-600 at 22-28px) rather than the 700+ of fintech/enterprise systems. Inter is the documented open-source substitute.

nodes.label: Photography-Led Visual Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: The system trusts photography and whitespace for visual heft instead of typographic muscle — which is WHY the homepage h1 sits at only 28px/700 and the listing h1 at 22px/500. The single loud typographic moment is the 64px rating display, because rating numbers are the peak trust signal.

nodes.label: Soft Shape Language (rounded scale)
nodes.rationale: 8px buttons, ~14px cards, fully-pill search bar, circular orbs/hearts. There is essentially no hard corner anywhere except the body grid — every interactive element is rounded, which reads as friendly and human.

nodes.label: Single Elevation Tier
nodes.rationale: One shadow definition plus a flat baseline — no progressive elevation tiers. Depth comes from photography, white-on-white surface separation and rounded-corner clipping instead of layered shadows.

nodes.label: Pill Search Bar + Rausch Search Orb
nodes.rationale: 64px fully-rounded white bar split by hairlines into Where/When/Who segments, terminated by a 48px circular Rausch orb — the hottest single color moment on the homepage and the most-tapped target.
nodes.norm_label: pill search bar + rausch search orb

nodes.label: Photo-First Property Card
nodes.rationale: 1:1 photo with rounded clipping, carousel dots, 'Guest favorite' badge top-left, heart top-right, then 4-5 meta lines. property-card-photo is split into its own token because wishlist/search surfaces reuse the photo plate without the meta block.

nodes.label: 64px Rating Display
nodes.rationale: The only place the system trusts type alone to carry hierarchy. Stars render in ink (#222222), not gold — a deliberate choice because yellow stars read as cheap in a travel context.

nodes.label: 8px Spacing System & Density Contrast
nodes.rationale: Sections get 64px of vertical air (tighter than the 80-96px typical of SaaS marketing) while card grids compress to 16px gutters — 'open hero, dense marketplace below'. Marketplace pages need card density per scroll.

nodes.label: Three-Product Top Nav (Homes / Experiences / Services)
nodes.rationale: Hand-illustrated 32px glyphs plus 'NEW' badges on the two newer products — signals a marketplace expansion rather than a feature dump.

nodes.label: Luxe / Plus Sub-Brand Accents
nodes.rationale: Luxe purple (#460479) and Plus magenta (#92174d) are scoped to sub-branded surfaces only and never appear in mainline marketing — preserving Rausch as the single brand voltage. Their full sub-systems are a documented gap.

nodes.label: Brenda Nunes Brand Identity System
nodes.rationale: A self-contained brand board (PT-BR) for a semijoias / jewelry brand: cover, logo versions, palette, typography, design system, mockups, developer tokens. Tagline 'Semijoias · Elegância · Exclusividade', dated 2025.

nodes.label: BN Monogram (SVG, 3 backgrounds + horizontal + icon)
nodes.rationale: Hand-drawn SVG serif B and N inside a double ring (solid r=44 + dashed r=41). Locked to two strokes only: gold #D4B483 on dark, ink #3A3A3A on light/rose. Shipped in stacked, horizontal (rule-separated) and icon-only lockups so it survives from favicon (16px) to cover (160px).

nodes.label: Rose / Gold / Off-White Palette
nodes.rationale: rose #E8C8D2 / rose-deep #D9B0BF / off-white #F7F3F1 / gold #D4B483 / gold-light #E8D5B0 / text #3A3A3A / text-light #8A7F7A / black #1A1A1A. Gold is reserved for accents, labels and hairlines rather than large fills — it acts as the luxury voltage against a warm off-white canvas.

nodes.label: Cormorant Garamond + Jost Type System
nodes.rationale: Cormorant Garamond (serif, weights 300-500) for display; Jost (geometric sans, weights 200-400) for body and UI. Everything runs at low weight with heavy uppercase letter-spacing (0.2em-0.35em) to read as editorial luxury rather than SaaS.

nodes.label: Brand Design System Components
nodes.rationale: Botões (primary / gold / outline / ghost), Formulários (underline-only inputs that shift the bottom border to gold on focus), Badges, Card de Produto (3:4 rose photo area), Espaçamentos and Bordas & Raios. Squared corners and borderless underline inputs are the deliberate anti-SaaS signature.

nodes.label: Brand Application Mockups
nodes.rationale: Pure-CSS mockups (no images) of packaging box, luxury bag, thank-you card, Instagram profile, product tag and favicon at 16/32/48px — proving the monogram scales across physical and digital touchpoints.

nodes.label: CSS Variable Tokens for Developers
nodes.rationale: The :root block (colors, --font-display/--font-body, --space-xs..2xl on a rem scale) is published as the handoff contract so the storefront can consume the brand without re-deriving values.
